prompt: What was wrong with how lesson 6's staging cleaned the prices?
hint: Did anybody learn what it fixed?

choices.text: It cleaned them wrongly
choices.why: The fixes were right.

choices.text: It was too slow for a thousand records
choices.why: Speed was not the problem.

choices.text: It did it silently, so nobody knew what it had fixed
choices.why: Right. The validator counts every fix.

choices.text: It could not read JSON
choices.why: It read it.

prompt: Why does the validator reject a missing price rather than fill it in?
hint: What would the filled value be?

choices.text: The database forbids nulls in that column
choices.why: The point is not the database.

choices.text: Nothing says what it should be, and a guess would load as a fact
choices.why: Right. Only certain fixes are made.

choices.text: Missing prices are always errors at the publisher, and the publisher always resends them
choices.why: Not always; the quarantine file is how Ana asks.

choices.text: To keep the batch under 5%
choices.why: The threshold is a separate rule.

prompt: A record arrives in currency `USD`. What does the validator do?

choices.text: Converts it to reais at today's rate
choices.why: That is a decision, not a certain fix.

choices.text: Stops the whole batch
choices.why: Only if more than 5% are rejected.

choices.text: Changes the currency to BRL and keeps the number
choices.why: That would keep a dollar price as reais.

choices.text: Rejects it, with the reason
choices.why: Right. currency 'USD'.

prompt: How many records did the validator reject from the real prices?

choices.text: So what the source sent is not confused with what the pipeline did

choices.text: Half-fixed records are larger

choices.why: It can.

choices.text: The loader reads the quarantine and needs the fields as they were sent

prompt: Half the records in a batch have no price. Why load none of them rather than the good half?
hint: Is what is left a smaller truth?

choices.text: PostgreSQL cannot load half a file
choices.why: It can.

choices.text: The good half is a false picture of the night, not a smaller true one
choices.why: Right. The batch is the problem.

choices.text: The good half is probably wrong too
choices.why: Each of its records passed.

choices.text: To save time
choices.why: Time is not the reason.

Why does the validator exit with status 1 when it stops?

choices.text: To delete the quarantine file
choices.why: The quarantine is kept.

choices.text: To retry the fetch, which Airflow does automatically when a step exits non-zero
choices.why: Retrying a broken export changes nothing.

choices.text: Python requires it after printing
choices.why: It does not.

choices.text: So the shell, make or Airflow stops the load after it

prompt: When does dbt check a model's contract?
hint: Before or after the table exists?

choices.text: Before building the table
choices.why: Right. The report keeps yesterday's table.

choices.text: After building, by reading the rows
choices.why: It never builds a mismatched table.

choices.text: Only in dbt test
choices.why: It is checked in run and build.

choices.text: When the report reads the table
choices.why: dbt is not involved in reading.

prompt: What does a contract on `daily_sales` not protect against?

choices.text: A column being renamed
choices.why: Names are in the contract.

choices.text: revenue_cents becoming a decimal number of reais
choices.why: That is exactly what it caught.

choices.text: Wrong numbers in a column of the right type
choices.why: Right. That is what tests are for.

choices.text: A column being dropped from the model's select
choices.why: The number of columns is checked.

choices.text: PostgreSQL refuses a null there from any writer

choices.text: Nothing; it is another test

choices.why: It refuses them.

choices.text: It makes the build faster

prompt: What makes the event volume check an expectation rather than a rule?

choices.text: It never fails
choices.why: It failed on the 20th.

choices.text: Some real days fall outside it

choices.text: It runs only once a week, on Mondays, after the backfill
choices.why: It runs in every build.

prompt: Why is the range half to double, and not ten per cent either way?

choices.why: The reason is real variation.
